promotions.set_note: Promoted 2026-07-29 (a-relations-wave7-v1, ladder (68)). Both recorded blockers are resolved. (1) The status cap: the target subfield:computer-systems was `proposed` when this edge was written and has since been promoted to `reviewed` under node-policy v1.4 (ACM CCS anchor, decision (102)) — clause 3 no longer blocks it. (2) The sourcing: two independent claim-stating articles now support it — enwiki First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC ("It contains the first published description of the logical design of a computer using the stored-program concept, which has come to be known as the von Neumann architecture") and enwiki Von Neumann architecture ("is a computer architecture based on the First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC , written by John von Neumann in 1945, describing designs discussed with John Mauchly and J."). The attribution dispute the original note flagged is preserved rather than resolved: the same source states "the name has become controversial due to von Neumann's failure to name other contributors", and the second names Mauchly and Eckert as participants in the designs discussed. That is a credit-and-share contest on top of an agreed authorship and influence — the existence-vs-share line of §8 clause-6 v2 — so it routes to supported plus this note, the same ruling shape applied to Einstein and relativity in person-wave11-v1 the same day. person:john-mauchly and person:j-presper-eckert are now corpus nodes (computing-wave1-v1, session #64), each carrying its own mirror of this edge (edge:john-mauchly-influenced-computer-systems, edge:j-presper-eckert-influenced-computer-systems, both reviewed 0.85) plus artifact-grain founder credit (edge:john-mauchly-founded-eniac, edge:j-presper-eckert-founded-eniac, both reviewed 0.9). Written with IDs rather than surnames on purpose: in prose this sentence was invisible to the stale-gap detector, which is how decision (121) found it while adjudicating the very question it records.
